title: FEVER: a large-scale dataset for Fact Extraction and VERification

title: FEVER: a large-scale dataset for Fact Extraction and VERification
question: 作者是如何证明所提方法有效的？
gold_answer: 作者通过实验评估来证明所提方法的有效性。具体包括：将标注的声明划分为训练集、开发集和测试集，并确保每个维基百科页面只出现在一个集合中；使用准确率评估3分类任务，对于SUPPORTED和REFUTED类别，要求提供句子级别的证据；通过计算预测句子与人工标注句子之间的F1分数来评估证据检索的正确性。

gold_evidence.text: We partitioned the annotated claims into training, development and test sets. We ensured that each Wikipedia page used to generate claims occurs in exactly one set.

Predicting whether a claim is SUPPORTED, REFUTED or NOTENOUGHINFO is a 3-way classification task that we evaluate using accuracy. In the case of the first two classes, appropriate evidence must be provided, at a sentence-level, to justify the classification.

We evaluate the correctness of the evidence retrieved by computing the F1-score of all the predicted sentences in comparison to the human-annotated sentences for those claims requiring evidence on our complete pipeline system (Section 5.7).

title: FEVER: a large-scale dataset for Fact Extraction and VERification
question: 这篇论文的主要贡献是什么？
gold_answer: 该论文的主要贡献是引入了一个公开可用的大规模数据集FEVER，用于从文本源中进行事实提取和验证。该数据集包含185,445个通过修改维基百科句子生成的声明，并由标注者分类为支持、反驳或信息不足。论文还开发了一个流水线方法，并展示了该数据集对声明验证任务的挑战性。

gold_evidence.text: In this paper we introduce a new publicly available dataset for verification against textual sources, FEVER: Fact Extraction and VERification. It consists of 185,445 claims generated by altering sentences extracted from Wikipedia and subsequently verified without knowledge of the sentence they were derived from. The claims are classified as SUPPORTED, REFUTED or NOTENOUGHINFO by annotators achieving 0.6841 in Fleiss κ.
Thus we believe that FEVER is a challenging testbed that will help stimulate progress on claim verification against textual sources.
In this paper we have introduced FEVER, a publicly available dataset for fact extraction and verification against textual sources.

title: Benchmarking and Bridging Emotion Conflicts for Multimodal Emotion Reasoning
question: 这篇论文报告了哪些关键实验结果？
gold_answer: 实验结果表明，MoSEAR在多个数据集上持续取得最先进性能，尤其在CA-MER基准的三个子集上表现突出。在CA-MER上，MoSEAR将音频对齐与视频对齐子集之间的差距从12%缩小到6%，展示了其缓解模态偏差的能力。在EMER数据集上，MoSEAR达到了60.58%的SoTA分数。在MER2023情感识别任务中，MoSEAR取得了最高F1分数，比之前的最先进模型Emotion-LLaMA高出9.4%。在DFEW数据集上，MoSEAR取得了最高UAR（64.26%），超越了专门的单任务模型。

title: Benchmarking and Bridging Emotion Conflicts for Multimodal Emotion Reasoning
question: 这篇论文的主要贡献是什么？
gold_answer: 本文的主要贡献包括：1）系统研究了情感多模态大语言模型在情感冲突场景下的表现，通过注意力分析揭示了模型对音频令牌的明显偏向，并发现视频与音频令牌数量极端不平衡是导致音频偏向的关键因素；2）提出了冲突感知多模态情感推理（CA-MER）数据集，包含视频对齐、音频对齐和模态一致三个子集，用于支持此类场景的评估；3）提出了MoSEAR框架，包含模态特定专家（MoSE）和注意力重新分配（AR）两个关键组件，分别用于训练时平衡视觉与非视觉模态、推理时校准冻结模型的注意力分布。

gold_evidence.text: In this paper, we present a systematic study of emotion MLLMs in the context of emotion conflicts. Our attention analysis on existing emotion MLLMs reveals a clear bias toward audio tokens, which impairs the integration of visual cues and results in inaccurate emotion reasoning. In addition, we find that the extreme imbalance between video and audio token counts is a key factor contributing to audio bias. To support evaluation in such scenarios, we introduce the Conflict-Aware Multimodal Emotion Reasoning (CA-MER) dataset, consisting of three subsets targeting video-aligned, audio-aligned, and modality-consistent cases. To mitigate this bias, we propose MoSEAR, a novel framework comprising two key components: (1) Modality-specific experts (MoSE), which balance visual and non-visual modalities during training; and (2) Attention reallocation (AR), which calibrates the frozen model’s attention distribution during inference.
